title: Home practical guide and safety card: balloon and bottle
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Reactivity (9F); energy transfer by heating
source: Written for science/y9 lesson 27 (Home practical guide and safety card: balloon and bottle (portal worksheet; warm tap water only, never heat sealed containers))
intro: Lesson 27: Gas pressure and physical change. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To see gas pressure change with temperature
equipment: Two bowls: warm tap water and cold water
safety: An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Stretch the balloon over the bottle neck
Stand the bottle in warm tap water for 2 minutes
Move it to cold water and watch again

questions.q: Heating a sealed gas makes the pressure...
Big question: why must aerosols stay below 50 °C?
questions.a: Heating raises the pressure inside until the can could burst.
